description: The Mobility Data Specification (MDS) is a set of application programming interfaces that standardise data sharing between cities and mobility providers so that cities can manage transport in the public right of way. It defines six APIs: provider (data pulled by agencies from operators, first released in June 2018), agency (data pushed by operators to agencies in real time), policy, geography, jurisdiction and metrics, and it covers modes such as dockless scooters and bicycles, mopeds, car share, sidewalk robots, shuttles, taxis and ride hailing. MDS was created by the Los Angeles Department of Transportation in 2018 and handed to the Open Mobility Foundation in November 2019; the README reports use by over 200 operators in over 1,200 cities. Coverage is global. The specification is free on GitHub under CC BY 4.0, with an OpenAPI schema for validation, and MDS feeds must also expose public GBFS or GOFS feeds. Caveats: it is a standard, not a dataset; data shared under MDS are held by cities and operators, not published by the foundation. MDS supports agent-based and demand models of micromobility, curb and right-of-way capacity planning and data pipelines for city digital twins. It complements the GBFS and GTFS specifications catalogued here.
